conditions.label: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, inferior wall

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3 months after the second MI.

Back to full duty per cardiology, which in January means the plow truck and the shop. No angina. No nitro. Some easy bruising on the forearms from the two antiplatelets, no other bleeding. Stools normal.

Smoking: says about half a pack on work days, more on weekends. Honest that it has crept back up.

Meds unchanged: ASA 81, clopidogrel 75, metoprolol succinate 25, atorvastatin 80, lisinopril 20, pantoprazole 40, NTG prn.
Allergy: blood products (AHTR 2024).

Exam: well. Regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Forearm bruises, scattered, small. No edema.

A/P
- CAD, old inferior MI x2, RCA stents x2: stable. Closed the acute STEMI entry; old MI and stent status remain. DAPT through October.
- Lipids/LFT/CBC today.
- HTN: at goal.
- Tobacco: counseled again; he will not take a medication. Left the door open.

RTC 3 months, can be video.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I need the pantoprazole and the metoprolol sent again, the pharmacy says no refills left. Same pharmacy. Thanks, Kevin

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Kevin, both sent this morning with refills through the year. They should be ready this afternoon.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he is in his truck on his lunch break, parked. Consent and identity confirmed.

Spring cleanups started. No chest pressure on the job, no shortness of breath beyond baseline, no lightheadedness. No bleeding. Taking all meds, the pill box is in the glovebox. Home BP readings he reads off his phone are in a good range.

Smoking about the same.

A/P: CAD s/p 2 RCA stents, stable. HTN controlled at home. No changes. Cardiology visit next month. In-person visit with labs in July.
Tobacco: brief counseling.

documents.title: Cardiology Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Routine follow-up for Kevin Allard: CAD with drug-eluting stents to the RCA in April and October 2025 after inferior STEMIs, LVEF 55%.

No angina, no nitroglycerin use, working full duty as a landscaping supervisor. Minor bruising only on dual antiplatelet therapy. Continues to smoke.

Examination unremarkable; blood pressure and heart rate at goal.

Plan: continue aspirin and clopidogrel through October 2026, then we will decide on single antiplatelet therapy. Continue metoprolol succinate 25 mg, atorvastatin 80 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, pantoprazole 40 mg. Smoking cessation again urged. Return in 6 months.

Allergies: blood products (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction).

Sincerely,
Outside cardiology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mid-summer check, labs drawn before the visit.

Heat has been rough on the crews; he is keeping himself to supervising and running the mower less. No chest discomfort with exertion, no nitro since he got the bottle. No palpitations, no syncope. Bruises easily, no other bleeding. Stomach quiet.

Still smoking. Asked him what would make the difference; he says maybe when the DAPT ends and he 'feels like a normal person again,' which I pointed out is backwards. He laughed.

Meds reviewed, unchanged. Allergy: blood products.

Exam: tan, comfortable. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Legs without edema, pedal pulses present.

A/P
1. CAD with old inferior MIs and RCA stents x2: stable on aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin 80, lisinopril, NTG prn. Clopidogrel end date is cardiology's call in October.
2. HTN: controlled.
3. Hyperlipidemia: lipids today.
4. Gastric ulcer hx: pantoprazole daily.
5. Tobacco use disorder: counseled; declines pharmacotherapy.
6. Health maintenance: LDCT due October, flu and COVID in the fall.

RTC October.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kevin, labs from Wednesday look good: kidney and liver tests normal on the atorvastatin, blood count normal on the two blood thinners, and your LDL is holding where we want it. No changes. See you in October.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request: clopidogrel 75 mg #90. On active list, seen 7/22. Sent with no additional refills since cardiology will decide on continuing past October; note to pt via pharmacy.
